parts.text:
{
  "first_impression": "This is genuinely charming and way more mechanically thoughtful than I expected from a cozy itch.io title. It nails the authentic highland shepherd fantasy without feeling like a boring chore simulator.",
  "scores": {
    "visual_appeal": 8,
    "readability": 7,
    "game_feel": 8,
    "fun_factor": 8,
    "variety": 9,
    "sense_of_progression": 8,
    "want_to_keep_playing": 9,
    "would_wishlist": 9
  },
  "best_things": [
    "The core flocking physics and Pip's stalking/creeping mechanics feel authentic to actual border collie sheepdog work rather than generic arcade pushing.",
    "The mission variety is surprisingly deep, throwing in legit sheepdog trials, helper dogs to command, stubborn rams, swimming, and night wolf ambushes.",
    "The charm system and three-star objectives give genuine replay value and mastery goals beyond just scraping through the sunset timer."
  ],
  "worst_problems": [
    {
      "problem": "During high-stakes wolf snatches, the camera doesn't zoom out or re-frame, forcing you to sprint blindly while staring at distance text and minimap icons instead of the action.",
      "where": "04:08 - 04:18",
      "severity": "major",
      "suggestion": "Pull the camera back dynamically during sprint rescues so both Pip and the fleeing predator stay in frame."
    },
    {
      "problem": "The mist mechanic over-restricts visibility to Pip's tiny circle, turning wide pasture navigation into tedious squinting and slow crawling.",
      "where": "07:33 - 07:52",
      "severity": "major",
      "suggestion": "Let sheep silhouettes or sound ripples show through the fog outside the dog's direct reach ring so it feels like hunting by ear rather than bumping into walls."
    },
    {
      "problem": "Sheep bottlenecking at narrow pen gates can trigger jittery bouncing and sudden erratic turns right at the finish line.",
      "where": "00:28 - 00:30",
      "severity": "minor",
      "suggestion": "Give gate entrances a slight funnel attractor once the flock is facing directly into the opening."
    },
    {
      "problem": "Ground textures and foliage across the wider moors look noticeably flat and low-detail during long sprints between pastures.",
      "where": "05:46 - 05:54",
      "severity": "cosmetic",
      "suggestion": "Add more micro-elevation, varied grass tufts, or heather clumps to break up the barren yellow-green flats."
    },
    {
      "problem": "Commands for the second dog (Old Fly) feel under-telegraphed in the UI, making it easy to forget whether she is holding position or following.",
      "where": "03:24 - 03:30",
      "severity": "minor",
      "suggestion": "Add a clear visual status marker or leash icon over Fly showing her current stance."
    }
  ],
  "boredom_points": [
    "Slowly nudging small groups across empty fields when wolves haven't spawned yet (00:15 - 00:20).",
    "Combing the empty edges of the moor in thick fog trying to locate the last stray (08:44 - 08:59)."
  ],
  "confusions": [
    "The exact difference between staring down Old Angus with creep vs barking to turn him without getting charged (05:34 - 05:39).",
    "How wolf attack aggro priorities work when two wolves strike from opposite sides simultaneously (06:55 - 07:01)."
  ],
  "wish_list": [
    "A free-roam training field where you can practice trial gate courses and dog whistling commands at your own pace.",
    "Cosmetic dog customization (different coat colors, bandanas, or collie breeds like rough collies or kelpies).",
    "Weather variants like driving rain and snowdrifts that affect sheep movement speed and sound travel."
  ],
  "one_line_review": "Untitled Goose Game meets A Short Hike with sheep; tense, charming, and shockingly faithful to real sheepdog handling."
}
